# Following the Example of Geologists, Biologists and Philologists[^1]

Messrs. Dewey, Schiller and their allies, in reaching this general conception of all truth, have only followed the example of geologists, biologists and philologists. In the establishment of these other sciences, the successful stroke was always to take some simple process actually observable in operation and then to generalize it, making it apply to all times, and produce great results by summating its effects through the ages.

[^1]: [[@Pragmatism - William James]]
